subject.title: [Feature]: Native E2EE Browser Chat, No Third-Party Required

question: Should native browser-held E2EE chat become a core Gateway/WebChat capability now, or should maintainers first define plugin/Gateway seams for an external implementation?
rationale: The request fits security and first-run UX goals, but it changes key management, transcript semantics, routing, relay behavior, and the core/plugin boundary, which automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Sponsor core E2EE design
options.body: Keep the issue open and require a maintainer-owned Gateway/WebChat security design before any feature branch lands.

options.title: Define plugin-first seams
options.body: Keep the issue open but narrow it to the Gateway/browser APIs an external E2EE chat plugin would need.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Leave existing WebChat, device pairing, dmScope, and third-party E2EE channels as the supported paths until maintainers explicitly revisit native browser E2EE.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core E2EE design
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require a maintainer-owned Gateway/WebChat security design before any feature branch lands.

likelyOwner.reason: He already reviewed this item as a maintainer-facing product/security architecture question and has adjacent Gateway chat history; secops should be included for the security model.
